content.user_title: Manage Azure Blob Storage with Python
content.value_statement: Azure Blob Storage tasks require correct clients, authentication, and transfer patterns. This skill gives focused Python SDK guidance for containers, blobs, SAS URLs, async clients, and performance settings.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install azure-storage-blob and azure-identity packages.
Explains DefaultAzureCredential setup with Azure Blob account URLs.
Demonstrates creating containers and uploading blobs from files, bytes, and streams.
Covers downloading blobs to files, memory, and existing buffers.
Shows listing, walking, deleting, and configuring blob metadata.
Includes SAS token, async client, and concurrency guidance for Python workflows.
limitations: Requires an existing Azure Storage account and valid Azure credentials.
Does not create Azure subscriptions, accounts, roles, or network rules.
Examples must be tested against the target environment before production use.
Does not replace an Azure security review for sensitive data workloads.

use_cases.title: Add Blob Transfers
use_cases.description: Build Python upload and download flows for application files, exports, or user content stored in Azure Blob Storage.

use_cases.title: Organize Data Files
use_cases.description: List blobs by prefix, walk virtual folders, and manage metadata for batch processing or analytics pipelines.

use_cases.title: Tune Storage Workflows
use_cases.description: Apply async clients, concurrency settings, and short-lived SAS URLs for larger or more controlled storage operations.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up The SDK
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to install the Azure Blob Storage Python SDK and connect with DefaultAzureCredential.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Python project.

prompt_templates.title: Upload And Download Blobs
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me write a Python flow that uploads a local file and downloads a blob to a chosen path.

prompt_templates.title: List And Manage Blob Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through listing blobs by prefix, walking folders, setting metadata, and deleting selected blobs safely.

prompt_templates.title: Design A Production Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a secure Python blob workflow with SAS expiry, async clients, metadata, and concurrency for large files.

output_examples.input: Explain how to upload a local file to Azure Blob Storage.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the service client, blob client, file stream, overwrite setting, and validation points for a safe upload.

output_examples.input: Plan a download flow for a large blob.
output_examples.output: The response recommends streaming or buffered reads, a clear output path, concurrency settings, and checks for available disk space.

output_examples.input: Review how to share one blob temporarily.
output_examples.output: The response describes a short-lived SAS URL with limited permissions, a clear expiry time, and careful handling of the token.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential when possible instead of long-lived connection strings.
Grant SAS tokens the minimum permissions and shortest practical expiry.
Use streaming, readinto, and concurrency settings for large blob transfers.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode account keys, connection strings, or SAS tokens in source files.
Do not use full memory reads for large blobs without size checks.
Do not delete or overwrite blobs without explicit confirmation and recovery planning.

faq.question: What Azure library does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers the Azure Blob Storage SDK for Python, mainly azure-storage-blob with azure-identity authentication.

faq.question: Can it help with DefaultAzureCredential?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how DefaultAzureCredential connects a Python client to an Azure Storage account URL.

faq.question: Does it create Azure resources for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides SDK guidance, but you must provide the storage account, permissions, and environment configuration.

faq.question: Can it handle async blob operations?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes async client patterns for uploads and downloads using the Azure async SDK.

faq.question: Does it explain SAS tokens?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows read-only SAS token generation with an expiry and a blob URL format.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production code?
faq.answer: It is a reference for implementation, but production code still needs testing, monitoring, and security review.
